title: One accent colour with one meaning
statement: A film uses one accent colour, and each accent keeps one fixed meaning (for example one colour always means 'fixed', another always 'changing').
evidence: 10 of 16 round-7 films use one accent, including the 3 tier-A product films; round-8 film 02 (tier A) uses blue only; the 1.8M-view launch keeps lime for 'fixed' and blue-violet for 'changing'.

title: Grain over smooth dark gradients
statement: Put grain of at least 0.02 over soft blurs, vignettes and dark mesh gradients (luma about 25-110), or dither before the encode, so 8-bit steps stay under 4% of sampled frames.
evidence: own measurement: an 8-bit step is 1.1% luminance at luma 215 but 4.8% at luma 50 after an x264 encode.

sources.locator: Environment > Banding is a dark-midtone problem; Layers > meshGradient bands

notes: Merged: Delivered frames show no 8-bit staircases (warn at 4% of a frame, fail when frames at 20% or more are a quarter of samples); smooth gradients carry grain of at least 0.02 amplitude and TPDF dither of plus or minus 1 LSB as the last step. [measured; thresholds calibrated on pack renders (2% Weber visibility keeps bright demos clean, still flags dark soft ones on 8 of 12 and 9 of 12 frames); synthetic test: a posterised ramp fails, the same ramp with grain passes.] | Banding is a dark-midtone problem (roughly luma 25-110); a 10-bit master re-encoded to 8 bit by the platform can band after delivery. layers/finisher.js lintStack also warns 'dither off and no grain'. | Merged: Dark gradient plates carry grain (>= 0.02) or encode below CRF 23; eyes/banding warns at 4% and fails at 20% of sampled frames. [measured; 19 Oct run: banding failed on 24 of 44 renders (12 templates at both aspects), e.g. 12/12 sampled frames on a device teaser and 10/12 on a vlog.] | The check catches it; no template sets grain or a lower CRF by default, so the fix is prose-only. The 0.02 grain floor is the source eyes/manifest.json cites (gotchas).

title: Character comedy looks clean
statement: Character comedy and kids' spots use a bright saturated grade with no grain, no dust and a vignette of at most 0.06.
evidence: art-direction judgement in frame-design and the mime-style recipe in the visual research; the finish preset ships these values.

title: Withhold colour until the pivot
statement: Keep the problem section black-and-white and bring the first colour in on the pivot frame, together with the returning bass and the brand line.
evidence: One round-6 film graded tier B: the problem stays monochrome and the first colour (a rising ribbon) arrives with the bass on the brand line.
notes: The ribbon part exists; nothing checks that earlier frames are monochrome.

title: Concrete objects, not abstract AI imagery
statement: Show objects the story already has (a stamped page, a bill, a sent message, a lamp switched off), never node graphs, glowing threads, orbiting cards, floating UI or holograms.
evidence: Abstract AI imagery is named as a cause in a rejected launch film and as the 'AI slop' failure in the rubric's failure table.

sources.locator: The rules that held up in production, rule 9

title: Declare planned black in the plan
statement: Any planned black (e.g. the silence before a trailer title) is declared as a hold or dip in the plan; undeclared, eyes/frames fails it.
evidence: The 15 s trailer cut failed eyes/frames on 11 black frames at 13.1 s; trailers and the short film failed 'frames' in 6 more renders.
notes: cuts/trailer/silenceBeforeHit allows black picture; the plan must say so.

title: Two stylised effects per shot
statement: At most 2 stylised effects are active in a shot and one hero light effect (flare, god rays, glint); stacked spikes (chroma + leak + flash + shake) occur only on a designated hit frame, at most 1 per 2 s.
evidence: binding compositing rule set in the pack's visual research (starting values, not yet tuned against renders).

title: End card: logo, line, action
statement: An end card holds an unaltered logo, one line with exactly one accent word, one URL or action, and fine print; in 9:16 the stack sits between y 269 and 1248 with the URL above the bottom 35%.
evidence: pack end-card rule; the ad and character-spot templates render one *word* of the line in the accent.

enforce.default: templates/ad config.mjs brand.cta; templates/character-spot config.mjs brand.line

notes: The logo is never recoloured, stretched or given effects (brand layer above grain, no fx).

title: Composite the UI around the presenter
statement: In a founder-on-camera launch, the product appears as composited glass panels in the room around a locked shot, with at most 2 hard cuts in 80 s.
evidence: Round-8 film 02 (tier A, 5.5x) has 2 hard cuts in 82 s; all UI is composited glass on one continuous take.

title: Fade glass by blur, not opacity
statement: A frosted panel fades by its own blur and tint, never by opacity < 1, a filter, a mask or a blend mode on an ancestor, any of which stops the backdrop blur.
evidence: r78 lane: tested in real headless capture; a test pins the ancestor-opacity failure; in canvas or still SVG export the backdrop mode draws no blur.

sources.locator: How each part follows its spec (ui.glassPanel); Needed item 4 (gotchas)

notes: Use plate mode outside a DOM host.

title: Show the photoreal hero alone
statement: Show a photoreal 3D hero alone on a defocused background; drop any prop that renders below the hero's realism.
evidence: owner review: the hero read as photoreal, while the procedural props around it (desk, mug, laptop) did not.
notes: eyes/composition checks one hero per frame, not prop realism.

title: Type after grade, grain over type
statement: Composite optics (lens, chroma, bloom, halation, leaks) before the grade and vignette, story type after the grade and steady, dust and grain over the type, the brand layer above grain at exact hex with no effects, then bars, then dither last.

params.order: plate > optics > grade > vignette > story type > dust > grain > brand > bars > dither

evidence: pack stack contract implemented in the finisher; brand pixels must probe at exact hex plus or minus 1 after the whole chain.
notes: Type is never under bloom, halation or chroma unless it is in-world (a sign). Weave applies to the plate only.

title: Composite the mark into a real scene
statement: Show the logo or UI composited onto a surface in a real scene (window, billboard, screen) rather than as a bumper on a flat field.
evidence: A craft-only concept ad puts its mark on a train window; a saves-strong round-3 brand film puts its system on a billboard with a passer-by; a SaaS breakdown overlays UI cards on live action.

title: One entrance verb, some by cut
statement: Give each element one entrance verb (mask, slide, scale) and let some arrive by cut; everything fading in is a banned default that needs a written reason.
evidence: house banned default.
notes: Critic Motion row: eases with intent (snap, settle, glide, land), no linear drift. Same banned-defaults list: a centred title on a gradient, glow on UI, decorative corner labels.

title: Never letterbox a vertical frame
statement: Never letterbox 9:16; bars appear only when the plan asks for them, and unplanned bars warn at 2% of a side and fail at 15% of the frame.
evidence: pack format rule (letterboxing 9:16 wastes pixels); eyes flags persistent near-black edge bars not named in the plan.
notes: Letterbox heights for 16:9 at 1920x1080: 2.39:1 = 138 px each, 2.00:1 = 60 px, 1.85:1 = 21 px; bars sit above grain.

title: One accent, at most 10% area
statement: Use one saturated accent hue, covering at most 10% of the frame area, alongside at most 3 base hues; state colours (success, warning) are the only extra hues and still need 3:1 against their background.
evidence: pack colour-discipline rule from frame-design and the 3D premium-look rules.
notes: contrast.py checks the 3:1 state-colour pairs; nothing measures accent area, so the 10% cap is prose-only. | Merged: Use one display face, one UI face and one accent colour, and apply the accent to every source (duotones, pills, logo, one word tint) so mixed media reads as one film. [craft; A practitioner house rule plus two craft-only films (a manifesto using one accent across archive, grid, type and logo; a concept ad with one brand colour).] | A demo inside the film may use its own client palette, kept apart from the frame's palette (a SaaS breakdown, reach unverified). | Merged: Keep every frame in one colour world (one field colour plus one accent) and let the product's own screens supply the variety. [measured-A; 3 of 3 tier-A video films: pale blue with one blue accent and one warm note; black and white with one blue glyph; one cobalt gradient with one lilac note.]

title: One grade per piece
statement: A piece uses one grade or one LUT (never both stacked); at most 2 grades by scene, joined by a 12-frame crossfade; log footage goes through a log-to-709 LUT first.
evidence: pack look rule; the grade is a closed-form CDL function emitted as a 33^3 cube, so no downloaded LUT pack is needed.
notes: frame-design says one grade per piece; visual.md allows 2 per piece by scene with a 12-frame crossfade. No lint counts grades.

title: One hero per key frame
statement: Every key frame names one hero (plus one support and texture); no second focal point holds 80% or more of the hero's saliency on more than 30% of key frames.
evidence: pack art-direction rule; the eyes saliency proxy warns when a competing blob reaches 80% of the strongest on 30% of 12 key frames.
notes: The check is a proxy: it counts competing focal points but does not know which one is the hero, and text counts as a focal point.

title: One bloom, vignette, grain
statement: Each frame carries exactly one bloom, one vignette and one grain; a plate that already bakes one sets plate.baked and the finisher skips it.
evidence: binding compositing rule; layers/finisher.js lintStack and layers/overlay.js lintOverlayStack warn on doubled grain, vignette or bloom.
notes: The lints exist as library functions but are not wired into mp check or any template build (grep finds no caller).

title: Measure every palette, defaults too
statement: Run the WCAG checker on every palette, including template defaults and published palettes, and fix every failing pair before the build.
evidence: 155 of 161 palettes in a popular open collection failed AA on at least one text pair; a shipped template's default success colour measured 1.72:1 on its own stage.
notes: contrast.py moves only CIELAB lightness of the failing foreground and prints the nearest passing hex. The colour-blind pass (a11y/colour-blind) belongs to the same QA step.

title: The product acts first
statement: The product's first appearance is UI acting on itself (a field typing, a window drawing, a card swapping), with no explainer card before it.
evidence: 6 of 8 round-8 films, including tier-A films 02, 07, 08 and 09 (the last three small samples).

title: Product hero at 36-46% width
statement: A product hero fills about 36-46% of the frame width on a long lens (18-22 degree field of view), with quiet negative space where the type will sit; move the product, not the type.
evidence: house default from product-shot reviews of rendered hardware; adjust by eye.
notes: visual.md: wide lenses over 35 degrees read game or toy unless intentional.

title: Composite real UI, never generate
statement: Never let an image or video model draw UI, text, logos or clock faces: generate the scene with a flat #00FF00 screen, detect its 4 corners, perspective-warp the real screenshot onto it, remove spill, and label it as real screens in a generated setting.
evidence: observed in production renders: image models returned real interface labels as near-words; the pack rule followed.

sources.locator: Never let an image model redraw UI or text

notes: Do not mention green objects in the prompt; keep raw scenes so a re-composite costs nothing. Invented numbers on a demo screen are changed in the product (demo data), not blurred. | Merged: Show real product screens composited into generated scenes, or a labelled placeholder; never let an image model redraw UI or text, and verify every on-screen AI answer. [house; image models garble UI text (own experience); in one 2024 hardware launch, wrong answers on screen were the focus of press coverage.] | Invented UI is a banned default.

title: Keep every text box in safe zone
statement: Every text box, including placeholder tags, speaker tags, watermarks and end titles, sits inside the platform safe rectangle (tall: top 0.14, bottom 0.35, sides 0.06 of the frame).
evidence: 19 Oct run: 20 of 44 renders put a tag, caption or title outside the safe area; misses measured 11-23 px (placeholder tag), 14 px (detail line), 30-196 px (speaker tag + caption row), and an end title touching the left edge.

title: Zoom tall UI to readable regions
statement: On 9:16 each product window zooms to its readable region; a whole-screen view (a payoff split, a wide builder) stays too small, and captions must not sit over the windows.
evidence: Saas lane stills: whole-screen 9:16 views read small; explainer captions sat over the windows; 9:16 renders failed eyes/readability on 19 Oct.

sources.locator: What is weaker than I would like

notes: A centre-reframed 16:9 plate also loses its sides on 9:16 (editable lane); a per-aspect source is not in the schema yet.

title: Text contrast at least 4.5:1
statement: On-screen text measures at least 4.5:1 against the pixels behind it after the grade (3.0-4.5 warns, under 3.0 fails); large text and UI graphics need at least 3:1.
evidence: WCAG 2.x 1.4.3 / 1.4.11 minimums adopted as floors for video; eyes measures the decoded backdrop at its 5th and 95th percentile.

sources.locator: 4. Contrast: the maths and the video cases

notes: Without the plan's fg colour eyes estimates the text colour and caps a contrast failure at a warning. Thin weights need more than the minimum.

title: Measure captions on worst frames
statement: Text over footage is measured against the lightest and the darkest frames it crosses, not the average; when it fails, add a solid box or pill, a 40-60% scrim, or an outline stroke of about 8% of font size plus a hard shadow.
evidence: practitioner fix order in the pack's type-and-colour reference; caption styles ship strokes of 0.03-0.07 em.

sources.locator: 4. Contrast: the maths and the video cases

notes: docs/research/visual.md 4.2 gives stroke 6% of font size or a 12 px shadow at 60% black; the frame-design reference gives about 8%. The 8% value is kept (later, matches the impact caption style 0.07).

title: Two worlds: story warm, product white
statement: A story-led launch film splits into warm low-key footage for the story and near-white pages with black sentence-case type for the product.
evidence: Measured palette shares of the tier-A* hero (distribution-assisted): near-black 28% across the sheet, near-white pages 44%; round-8 film 03 (boosted-looking) uses the same warm-human / cold-software split.
